newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market continued steady on Friday despite a further reduction in liquidity, dealers said.
They added however that the benchmark treasury bill rate had eased at Thursday's weekly tender in spite of the cash shortage characteristic of the whole week.

"I expected it to go up but maybe (it did not) because the market shortage is likely to be short-lived," one dealer said, adding a number of treasury bill maturities were coming up the following week.

The treasury bill rate moved a few points down to 17.88 percent on Thursday from last week's 17.90 percent, but on Friday discount houses were selling the central bank paper unchanged at 17.85 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were also being bought and sold at a steady 18.75 and 18.50 percent respectively while call money held to the previous day's 18.50 percent.

Negotiable certificates of deposit maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted stable at 19.25 percent (buying) and at 18.75 percent (selling) in a market which was indicated Z$13 million short, from a surplus of Z$11.3 million last time.
